clue.text: Early 6 with 9 24 16

blocks.note: surface reading: an early form of travel, the answer to 6 down
setter's reading: the vehicle Henry Ford offered in any colour so long as it was black, the long answer at 9

explanation.walkthrough: The clue is made entirely of cross-references: 6 is TRANSPORT, and 9, 24 and 16 together make Ford's famous line, so the answer is the car it described, the MODEL T.
explanation.definitionFit: Ford's mass-produced car of 1908 was early motor transport, famously sold only in black paint.

clue.text: Roof piece touching around radius

indicators.note: around means wrapped about something placed in its middle

blocks.note: a chessman or draughtsman is a piece
touching in the sense of moving, pitiful
R is the abbreviation for radius

explanation.surface: A section of roof is in contact with the edge of a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A mansard is a roof with two slopes on each side, the lower one steep, named after François Mansart.

clue.text: Do Everton call Arsenal, League leaders, for a transfer?

indicators.note: leaders are the ones at the front, so only the opening letter of each word counts

blocks.note: first letters of the five words

explanation.surface: A football question: will Everton ring Arsenal about buying a player?
explanation.walkthrough: The transfer is not a football signing but a picture applied by pressing it on, as in a transfer sheet.
explanation.definitionFit: A decal is a printed design that is moved onto a surface, which in Britain is called a transfer.

clue.text: Langtry's apartment in Monet's garden?

definitions.note: describes where the thing is found rather than naming it

blocks.note: Lillie Langtry, the Victorian actress, was the Jersey Lily
a pad is slang for a flat

explanation.surface: The actress Lillie Langtry seems to have a flat in the painter's garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Monet painted the water lilies in his pond at Giverny over and over, so the leaf they float on belongs there.
explanation.definitionFit: The floating leaves of water lilies fill the pond in Monet's garden at Giverny, which he painted repeatedly.

clue.text: Saw Little Richard in Wales with Little Mary

blocks.note: Dic is the Welsh pet form of Richard, as in the rebel Dic Penderyn
Little Mary is an old euphemism for the stomach, from a J. M. Barrie play

explanation.surface: The rock'n'roller Little Richard turns up in Wales alongside a girl called Mary.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Richard and Little Mary both look like people; one is the Welsh short form of a name and the other a coy word for the belly.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or maxim, and a dictum is likewise a pronouncement or proverb.

clue.text: 1 across ruined in crash!

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so this word's own letters are broken up and reformed
in places one item within another

blocks.note: the earlier answer is the MODEL T, often called simply the T
the word itself, to be scrambled

explanation.surface: An old Ford car is wrecked in a smash.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruined does double duty: its letters are rearranged around the T of the car.
explanation.definitionFit: To crash a party or event is to turn up uninvited, which is to intrude.

clue.text: Perhaps a Tolpuddle Martyr's ecstasy?

definitions.note: possessive standing for that Martyr's sentence, a noun

blocks.note: first meaning: the penal exile to Australia given to the Dorset farm labourers of 1834
second meaning: a rapturous state, being carried away

explanation.walkthrough: The Tolpuddle Martyrs were Dorset farm workers sentenced to be shipped to Australia for forming a union.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both deportation of convicts overseas and an overwhelming feeling of delight or rapture.

clue.text: Game speech from Erica's mother

indicators.note: in speech, what counts is how the words come out of the mouth rather than their spelling

blocks.note: Erica Jong is the American novelist, so her mother would be Ma Jong

explanation.surface: A game is played on words spoken by a novelist's mother.
explanation.walkthrough: Erica Jong wrote Fear of Flying; her mum, Ma Jong, sounds like the tile game.
explanation.definitionFit: Mah-jong is a Chinese tile game for four players, so it is a game by name.

clue.text: You can rest here, old thing!

definitions.text: You can rest here, old thing!

blocks.note: surface reading: a friendly invitation to sit down and relax
setter's reading: addressed to an antique, offering it a place where old objects are kept for display

explanation.walkthrough: 'Old thing' sounds like a fond way to address a friend; here it is literally an old object, and the place it rests is where artefacts are shown.
explanation.definitionFit: A public institution where historic objects and artefacts are kept and displayed for visitors.

clue.text: The 1across 4: "Alas! Auto's lacking cool tints."  Henry: "So what? B____ off!"

annotation.answer: ANY COLOUR THAT HE WANTS SO LONG AS IT IS BLACK

indicators.note: being told to clear off sends the preceding letters scattering into a new order

blocks.note: the complaint, every letter used
the name taken as written
the retort up to the initial of the rude word, taken as written

explanation.surface: A buyer moans that the car comes in no nice colours, and Henry Ford tells them rudely to go away.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1across 4 is the MODEL T DICTUM; all 37 letters before 'off' rearrange into Ford's line, and the blanked swear word contributes only its B.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Ford's famous saying about his Model T, that buyers could have any paint they liked provided it was black.

clue.text: Beer's a barrier to work

blocks.note: a wall is a barrier
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Drinking beer gets in the way of doing your job.
explanation.walkthrough: Wallop is British slang for beer; OP is the standard abbreviation of opus, a musical work.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal British usage wallop means beer or ale, especially cheap strong stuff.

clue.text: Decorator's suspension

definitions.note: a possessive standing for the decorator's paint, a noun

blocks.note: first meaning: the water-based paint a decorator puts on walls
second meaning: in chemistry, fine droplets of one liquid dispersed in another

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like a decorator being suspended from work; the possessive just means the decorator's paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Emulsion is both everyday wall paint and a scientific term for one liquid dispersed through another.

clue.text: Attachment of a theologian to the last expressed uncertainty

blocks.note: taken as written
DD is a Doctor of Divinity
the end is the last part
um is the noise of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A theologian is attached to a final, hesitant remark.
explanation.definitionFit: An addendum is material added on to a document, so it is a kind of appendix or attachment.

clue.text: Smattering of such strategy lacked by General Stanley

definitions.text: Smattering of such strategy lacked by General Stanley

blocks.note: surface reading: a general who knows little tactics
setter's reading: completes the line from the Major-General's song in The Pirates of Penzance

explanation.walkthrough: Major-General Stanley in Gilbert and Sullivan sings that he will be the best general once he has 'a smattering of ... strategy'; the missing adjective is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemental means basic or rudimentary, which is the kind of strategy the comic general admits he does not yet have.

clue.text: Garden ought to yield "an elegant sufficiency"

indicators.note: the words themselves are made to give up the letters they already contain

blocks.note: the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: A garden should produce food in genteel plenty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I have had an elegant sufficiency' is a mock-genteel way of saying you have eaten enough.
explanation.definitionFit: The quoted phrase is a jocular polite formula for having had as much food as one needs.

clue.text: Composer left one to gain another

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
Roman numeral one
to get is to gain
another one, again the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A composer quits one post in order to land a different one.
explanation.definitionFit: György Ligeti was a Hungarian-born composer of modern music, known for pieces used in 2001: A Space Odyssey.

clue.text: See 9
I'm through with this. No, I'm not!

definitions.note: an exclamation standing for the deadlock where one cannot get through, a noun

blocks.note: taken as written
passé means finished, through

explanation.surface: Someone declares they are quitting, and someone else flatly refuses to give way.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sentence builds the word, I'm plus passé; the reply 'No, I'm not' is the stalemate where nobody gets through.
explanation.definitionFit: An impasse is a deadlock or dead end, a place or situation where progress is blocked.

clue.text: Euthanasia author''s final blow: "Let's restore 'er!"

indicators.note: to restore is to put back together, so these letters are rebuilt in a fresh order

blocks.note: a knockout, the blow that ends a fight
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An advocate of assisted dying is pictured at a deathbed, urging that a woman be revived.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Koestler, author of Darkness at Noon, was a vice-president of the Voluntary Euthanasia Society and took his own life.
explanation.definitionFit: The writer Arthur Koestler published a pamphlet on self-deliverance and campaigned for voluntary euthanasia, ending his own life in 1983.

clue.text: Period in Malaysia's capital for a Malayalam state

indicators.note: in means placed inside something else

blocks.note: KL is the usual short form of Kuala Lumpur
an era is a period
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spell in Kuala Lumpur, apparently, is spent in a southern Indian state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Malaysia's capital' tempts one to take the first letter M; it means the city, Kuala Lumpur, shortened to KL.
explanation.definitionFit: Kerala is the Indian state on the Malabar coast where Malayalam is the main language.

clue.text: Selectively reproduced info from Brussels, I see

blocks.note: Brussels is the seat of the European Union
gen is British slang for information
I see read as letter sounds

explanation.surface: Information copied selectively out of Brussels, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen is British slang for information, as in 'get the gen'.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugenic relates to improving a population by controlled, chosen breeding.

clue.text: Snooty detachment making priest sit up before Mass

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible
taken as written
M is the abbreviation for mass

explanation.surface: Aloof behaviour leads a priest to sit upright before the service.
explanation.walkthrough: Eli is the crossword's stock priest; 'before' places the reversed word ahead of the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Elitism is the attitude of a superior group holding itself apart from others, a haughty aloofness.

clue.text: Alumnus with short fuse to yield obedience in Scotland

blocks.note: OB is an old boy, a former pupil
a short fuse is a quick temper

explanation.surface: A hot-headed former pupil is made to submit.
explanation.walkthrough: OB, old boy, is the British term for a former pupil of a school.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtemper is a Scots legal word meaning to comply with a court order or judgment.

clue.text: Anti-Renaissance type arrived here once

blocks.note: got there means arrived
hic is Latin for here, the language of old

explanation.surface: Someone opposed to the Renaissance showed up here long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: Gothic or blackletter type is the medieval script that Renaissance roman lettering replaced.
explanation.definitionFit: Gothic is the heavy medieval typeface that humanist printers of the Renaissance rejected in favour of roman.

clue.text: Thentient Thcottish Thuperior

blocks.note: a sentient being is sane, and sane said with this lisp turning s into th comes out as the spoken form

explanation.walkthrough: Every word is lisped: Sentient Scottish Superior. A thane was a Scottish lord, and 'sane' (of sound mind, like sentient) said with a lisp sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A thane was a Scottish feudal lord ranking below an earl, as in Macbeth, Thane of Cawdor.

clue.text: See 9
Good shape from Scottish sartor?

blocks.note: first meaning: proper working order
second meaning, playful: a maker of kilts, as a tailor makes suits

explanation.walkthrough: Sartor is a rare word for a tailor; the question mark flags that the second meaning is an invented word.
explanation.definitionFit: Kilter means proper condition or balance, used mostly in 'out of kilter'.

clue.text: Society's upper crust? Munch on this?

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for society
the cream is the elite, the upper crust

explanation.surface: High society's posh pastry crust invites a bite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Munch' is not chewing: it is Edvard Munch, who painted The Scream.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norwegian painter Edvard Munch worked on The Scream, his most famous canvas.
